blocking: A project whose web scripts are all legacy plugin site apps gets told to create its first one, and loses access to the scripts running on its site today. This counts only site_app hog functions, but the scene it gates also lists plugin-backed site apps loaded from pipeline_frontend_apps_configs and passed in as manualFunctions. Those projects count zero, and skippable: false means there's no way to the list or the History tab. The loader that fetches them still calls the migration "super temporary", so these projects are expected to exist.

This comment says the leader's healer clears a ghost fence on observation, but maybe_heal is only called from the property-write path and from fold_person_document — fence_person's rejection branch returns fenced_status(...) without calling it. So the one caller that observes the ghost fence repeatedly (this retry loop) can never trigger the heal, and for a low-traffic person nobody else will either. The seal step then retries forever, and since this op already holds marks on its target and other sources, those persons are stuck too.
Concrete way to get a ghost: an op releases a fence with Abo

suggestion: psak_allowed_actions is read here via getattr(view, "psak_allowed_actions", None) or [], but ScopeBasePermission declares scope_object_read_actions and scope_object_write_actions as class-level attributes with empty-list defaults. The next person adding a PSAK-supporting viewset has to know psak_allowed_actions exists; right now it's discoverable only by reading this branch.
Declare it on the base so the convention sits next to the related allowlists:
class ScopeBasePermission(BasePermission):
    write_actions: list[str] = ["create", "update", "partial_update", "patch", "destroy"]
